clue.text: Athletic activity thus deformed toe

definitions.meaning: a field event in which a heavy ball on a wire is thrown
a toe bent permanently downward at the middle joint is known by this name

explanation.surface: An athlete's sporting pursuit has left them with a misshapen toe.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing the weighted ball is a track-and-field event, and a clawed toe deformity carries the same tool's name.

clue.text: I piled into a chap with force

indicators.note: the letter I crashes into the middle of the following words, so it is put inside them

parts.note: a chap is a man

explanation.surface: Someone forcefully crashed into a fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb meaning with full force or vehemently, as in sailors heaving at the ropes.

clue.text: Friend gets another entangled in scheme

indicators.note: the second friend gets caught up inside the first, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a mate is a friend
another friend: china, from rhyming slang 'china plate' for mate

explanation.surface: A friend draws another pal into a scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' stands for mate, so CHINA is a second word for friend; 'gets' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To machinate is to plot or scheme, the verb sense of the clue word.

clue.text: Jog, but tear across fast road

indicators.note: the word for tear stretches across the road, enclosing it

parts.note: to rend is to tear
the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI in crosswords

explanation.surface: Someone out jogging rips across a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jog' looks like running, but it is the memory sense; the M1 is the London-to-Leeds motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To jog someone's memory is to prompt them, which is what reminding does.

clue.text: General secures unit some drink

indicators.note: the general's name holds the unit fast inside it

parts.note: Robert E. Lee, Confederate general
a monad is a single unit

explanation.surface: A general obtains a supply of drink for his unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemonade is a soft drink, a type of beverage.

clue.text: Very quickly take to a pet that's in pain

parts.note: to take to something is to like it
scalded, burnt by hot liquid, so hurting
a cat is a household pet

explanation.surface: Someone warms to a pet that is suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are taken in answer order: 'that's in pain' describes the pet and comes before it in the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for moving off at great speed, like a burnt animal bolting.

clue.text: It's the moment for some gospel but fail to come forward

definitions.text: It's the moment for some gospel
definitions.meaning: read cryptically: the hour for reading St Mark's Gospel
to march on the spot, making no progress

explanation.surface: A churchgoer says it is time for scripture but then hangs back.
explanation.definitionFit: Marching on the spot without advancing is the idiom; cryptically, it is the occasion for the second Gospel.

clue.text: Nick's 100 mph companion?

definitions.note: the 's stands for is: nick is a small cut or groove, and the possessive is read as 'is'

parts.note: 100 mph is a ton-up; in a down clue the ton is written upward, giving the letters reversed
CH is the abbreviation for Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: A question about the companion who rides with someone named Nick at a ton.
explanation.walkthrough: A ton-up is motorcycle slang for 100 mph; in a down entry 'ton up' reads TON upwards, so the speed itself supplies the reversed letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A notch is a small V-shaped cut, the same thing as a nick in wood or a blade.

clue.text: Can the old play in this competition?

indicators.note: the letters of these words are allowed to play, shifting into a new order

explanation.surface: A question whether older people can take part in a sporting contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A ten-event athletics contest, the competition the clue points at.

clue.text: One brings together 1 and 10, somehow

indicators.note: the combined letters are arranged in some other way

parts.note: refers to the answer at 1 across
refers to the answer at 10 across

explanation.surface: Someone combines two numbered items in some fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers point to other answers: 1 across and 10 across, whose letters are combined and rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A matchmaker arranges romantic pairings, bringing people together.

clue.text: Nail down policy

definitions.meaning: to fasten with a small nail
a course of action or approach

explanation.surface: Fix a policy firmly in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A tack is a short nail and also a line of approach, as in trying a different course.

clue.text: Popular move gains one badge

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: the letters are moved around into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A crowd-pleasing manoeuvre earns someone a badge.
explanation.definitionFit: Insignia are badges or emblems of rank or membership.

clue.text: I am grateful to encounter island — this one?

definitions.text: I am grateful to encounter island — this one?

parts.note: ta is an informal British thank-you
to hit upon is to encounter

explanation.surface: A traveller gives thanks on reaching an island and wonders which one it is.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British slang for thanks. The whole clue also serves as the definition: this is an island that a grateful traveller reaches.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahiti is a Pacific island in French Polynesia, the island the clue suggests.

clue.text: Having run, not quite catch song of bird

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for run in cricket

indicators.note: the last letter is left off

parts.note: to catch a song is to hear it

explanation.surface: After a jog, someone barely makes out a bird's song.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large flightless South American bird.

clue.text: I may need this to protect cut in side in hospital, please

definitions.text: I may need this to protect cut

parts.note: side, as in putting on side, means airs or pretension
pray means please, as in 'pray be seated'

explanation.surface: A patient with a cut on their side in hospital asks for something to protect it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' reads as a wound, but it means a haircut; 'side' is the old sense of pretension, airs.
explanation.definitionFit: Spray lacquer holds a styled haircut in place, so someone fresh from the barber may want it.

clue.text: One coat, reversible; only woman could wear it

indicators.note: the coat is turned around, so its word reads the other way

parts.note: a mac is a raincoat
the Roman numeral for one
sole means only

explanation.surface: A reversible coat is described as one only a woman could wear.
explanation.definitionFit: A camisole is a woman's loose sleeveless undergarment.

clue.text: Chic nurse sporting this?

indicators.note: the letters sport about, rearranging into a new word

explanation.surface: A stylish nurse might be wearing this item.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrunchie is a fabric-covered elastic band for tying back hair, the sort a smart nurse would wear.

clue.text: In a state, as banker goes bust

indicators.note: the letters break apart and reassemble in a new order

explanation.surface: In some state, a banker goes bankrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebraska is a US state in the Great Plains.

clue.text: Measured by stars, team's serious

parts.note: a side is a team; the possessive is no letter
real can mean serious or genuine

explanation.surface: A team's seriousness is gauged by its star players.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidereal time is reckoned from the apparent motion of the stars, not the sun.

clue.text: Leaving peak, mountain stream makes breach

indicators.note: the peak departs from the stream's word, so it is removed

parts.note: a torrent is a rushing mountain stream
a tor is a rocky hill or peak

explanation.surface: A stream leaving a summit cuts a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A rent is a tear or split, a breach in fabric or relations.

clue.text: Family with five daughters inclined to accept extremes of noise

indicators.note: the word for inclined takes in the letters, holding them inside

parts.note: bent means inclined, as in having a bent for something

indicators.note: the first and last letters of the word noise

explanation.surface: A large family of girls tends to put up with a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: The family is the one in Jane Austen's Pride and Prejudice, with daughters Jane, Elizabeth, Mary, Kitty and Lydia.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr and Mrs Bennet of Pride and Prejudice have five daughters, a literary reference.

clue.text: An acid shortly eats line in stone

indicators.note: the shortened word swallows the line, taking it inside
the last letter is cut off

parts.note: sharp means acid in taste

explanation.surface: Acid quickly corrodes a line cut in stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' cuts the P from SHARP, leaving SHAR; 'eats' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashlar is finely dressed building stone cut into square blocks.

clue.text: Thrust head out of dive

indicators.note: the first letter is taken away

parts.note: a plunge is a dive

explanation.surface: Someone drives their head out of a dive.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunge is a sudden forward thrust, as in fencing.

clue.text: Sort of ring the poet palmed in an hour?

definitions.meaning: a band set all round with gems, symbolising endless love

definitions.text: the poet palmed in an hour?
definitions.meaning: Blake wrote of holding infinity in the palm of your hand and this in an hour

explanation.surface: A ring the poet held in his hand within an hour.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is William Blake's Auguries of Innocence: 'Hold Infinity in the palm of your hand / And Eternity in an hour.'
explanation.definitionFit: An eternity ring has an unbroken circle of stones; Blake's line holds endless time in an hour.

clue.text: Time erodes totem pole

indicators.note: wearing away the outer letters leaves a word lodged within the phrase

explanation.surface: Weathering wears away a carved pole over time.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempo is speed or pace, a musical sense of time.

clue.text: Refuse to add name to garment

parts.note: a bra is an undergarment

explanation.surface: Someone declines to sew a name label into clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Bran is the husk separated from grain, waste or refuse.

clue.text: Not quite winning race one enters on holiday?

definitions.meaning: a property one goes into when away on a break

explanation.surface: Someone narrowly misses victory in a holiday race.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday property besides one's main residence; also finishing runner-up past the line.

clue.text: Prepare theatre programme in the usual parts

definitions.meaning: read cryptically: to type out the list of actors
always given the same kind of role

explanation.surface: An instruction to make the playbill for a show with standard roles.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor repeatedly given similar roles is typecast; cryptically, typing the cast list readies a programme.

clue.text: Everything that comes under the 1?

definitions.meaning: the whole amount, all of it
1 across is the auctioneer's tool; what goes under it at auction is an item for sale

explanation.surface: Asking whether everything goes under the hammer at once.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means all of it; at auction, each item sold under the gavel is a lot.
